name: Testaceous
lede: Testaceous is an old descriptive word for the reddish-brown of unglazed tiles and flowerpots, a color most people see every day without the word.

sections.title: The color of tile
sections.body:
Paterson defines testaceous as the reddish-brown colour of unglazed tiles or flowerpots, or brick-red or brownish-yellow [1]. A compound, fusco-testaceous, is listed with the meaning reddish brown [2].

The word is rare now, but it names a very common color [1]. Paterson's definition also allows brick-red or brownish-yellow, so the word covers a short range from reddish to yellowish, not one fixed shade, and the swatch here is just one point inside that range [1]. A flowerpot terracotta is the everyday version [1]. No book in the set tells a longer story about it, so this page stays short [1][2].  Because the color is that of fired clay, any terracotta pot in a garden is a ready sample of it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #CB8062 is a warm salmon-clay color [3]. It sits next to [[terracotta]], [[brick-red]] and [[tan]] [3]. Screen colors are approximate [3].
